audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition, with extensive Septuagint citation network; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Son as final speech, radiance/imprint language, purification, enthronement, and catena of Scripture citations.

verses.restored: In many parts and many ways long ago the Divine spoke to the ancestors in the prophets,

familiar.text: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,

modern.text: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.

original.text: Πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως πάλαι ὁ θεὸς λαλήσας τοῖς πατράσιν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις

verses.restored: but in these last days spoke to us in Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the ages.

familiar.text: Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;

modern.text: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.

original.text: ἐπʼ ἐσχάτου τῶν ἡμερῶν τούτων ἐλάλησεν ἡμῖν ἐν υἱῷ, ὃν ἔθηκεν κληρονόμον πάντων, διʼ οὗ καὶ ⸂ἐποίησεν τοὺς αἰῶνας⸃·

verses.restored: He, being radiance of glory and exact imprint of his reality, bearing all things by the word of his power, having made purification of sins/misalignments, sat down at right hand of Majesty on high,

familiar.text: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;

modern.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

original.text: ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ, φέρων τε τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως, ⸂διʼ αὑτοῦ⸃ καθαρισμὸν ⸂τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ποιησάμενος⸃ ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τῆς μεγαλωσύνης ἐν ὑψηλοῖς,

verses.restored: having become as much greater than the messengers as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs.

familiar.text: Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.

modern.text: So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.

original.text: τοσούτῳ κρείττων γενόμενος τῶν ἀγγέλων ὅσῳ διαφορώτερον παρʼ αὐτοὺς κεκληρονόμηκεν ὄνομα.

verses.restored: For to which of the messengers did he ever say: You are my Son; today I have begotten you? And again: I will be to him Father, and he will be to me Son?

familiar.text: For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?

modern.text: For to which of the angels did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father” ? Or again: “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son” ?

original.text: Τίνι γὰρ εἶπέν ποτε τῶν ἀγγέλων· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε, καὶ πάλιν· Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ εἰς πατέρα, καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι εἰς υἱόν;

verses.restored: And again, when he brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, he says: Let all messengers of Divine worship him.

familiar.text: And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.

modern.text: And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels worship Him.”

original.text: ὅταν δὲ πάλιν εἰσαγάγῃ τὸν πρωτότοκον εἰς τὴν οἰκουμένην, λέγει· Καὶ προσκυνησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι θεοῦ.

verses.restored: And concerning the messengers he says: The One making his messengers winds, and his servants flame of fire.

familiar.text: And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.

modern.text: Now about the angels He says: “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”

original.text: καὶ πρὸς μὲν τοὺς ἀγγέλους λέγει· Ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα, καὶ τοὺς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πυρὸς φλόγα·

verses.restored: But concerning the Son: Your throne, O Divine, is into the age of the age, and the scepter of straightness is scepter of your reign.

familiar.text: But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.

modern.text: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

original.text: πρὸς δὲ τὸν υἱόν· Ὁ θρόνος σου ὁ θεὸς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος, ⸂καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος τῆς εὐθύτητος⸃ ῥάβδος τῆς βασιλείας ⸀σου.

verses.restored: You loved righteousness/justice and hated lawlessness; because of this the Divine, your Divine, anointed you with oil of gladness beyond your companions.

familiar.text: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

modern.text: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”

original.text: ἠγάπησας δικαιοσύνην καὶ ἐμίσησας ἀνομίαν· διὰ τοῦτο ἔχρισέν σε ὁ θεός, ὁ θεός σου, ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους σου·

verses.restored: And: You, Lord, according to beginnings, founded the earth, and heavens are works of your hands.

familiar.text: And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands:

modern.text: And: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

original.text: καί· Σὺ κατʼ ἀρχάς, κύριε, τὴν γῆν ἐθεμελίωσας, καὶ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σού εἰσιν οἱ οὐρανοί·

verses.restored: They will perish, but you remain; and all will become old like garment,

familiar.text: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment;

modern.text: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.

original.text: αὐτοὶ ἀπολοῦνται, σὺ δὲ διαμένεις· καὶ πάντες ὡς ἱμάτιον παλαιωθήσονται,

verses.restored: and like robe you will roll them up, like garment they will be changed; but you are the same, and your years will not fail.

familiar.text: And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.

modern.text: You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed; but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”

original.text: καὶ ὡσεὶ περιβόλαιον ἑλίξεις αὐτούς, ⸂ὡς ἱμάτιον⸃ καὶ ἀλλαγήσονται· σὺ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς εἶ, καὶ τὰ ἔτη σου οὐκ ἐκλείψουσιν.

verses.restored: And to which of the messengers has he ever said: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies footstool of your feet?

familiar.text: But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?

modern.text: Yet to which of the angels did God ever say: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet” ?

original.text: πρὸς τίνα δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἴρηκέν ποτε· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου;

verses.restored: Are they not all serving spirits, sent out into service because of those about to inherit salvation/healing?

familiar.text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?

modern.text: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?

original.text: οὐχὶ πάντες εἰσὶν λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα εἰς διακονίαν ἀποστελλόμενα διὰ τοὺς μέλλοντας κληρονομεῖν σωτηρίαν;

translation_notes: Hebrews 1 is a Scripture-catena built largely from Greek Jewish Scriptures; citation texture should remain visible.
Son-language is enthronement/inheritance/revelation language, not anti-angel polemic detached from Jewish apocalyptic context.
Purification of sins is mentioned before priesthood is fully developed.
safety_note: Do not frame Hebrews as God replacing Judaism with Christianity. The chapter argues through Israel's own Scriptures about the Son's exalted identity.
